note: Facts transcribed by Claude from documents Charlie supplied on 2026-10-06 (docs/research/). Each item names its source. Not pulled data; quoted third-party research.

pragmata_calendar.source: Pragmata Partners, French Political and Fiscal Risk Calendar, prepared for Liminality, October 2026 (docs/research/pragmata-france-fiscal-policy-calendar-2026-10.pdf)
events: Assembly debates the revenue side of the 2027 budget
Assembly vote on the first part of the budget
Social Security funding bill vote; spending debate begins
Assembly vote on the full budget, first reading
European Commission autumn forecast and opinion under the excessive deficit procedure
Senate and the parliamentary shuttle; budget in place by 31 Dec, or a special law
Expected Cour de cassation ruling in the Le Pen case
ECB decision, between the two rounds

pragmata_budget_note.source: Pragmata Partners memo to Liminality, 30 September 2026, drawing on a Paris-based colleague (docs/research/pragmata-french-budget-negotiations-2026-10-01.pdf)
pragmata_budget_note.censure_arithmetic: 289 votes needed of 577; RN and allies 139, left excluding PS 126, non-affiliated 5 = 270; PS (68) or LR (48) decide

political_alpha.source: Political Alpha Research, 'France: The Budget Now Runs Through Le Pen', 5 October 2026 (docs/research/political-alpha-france-budget-2026-10.pdf)
political_alpha.lecornu_pledge: 17 September 2026: no 49.3 and no ordinances absent obstruction
political_alpha.socialists: all four left group leaders on record they would vote to censure
political_alpha.rn_position: Le Pen prefers an imperfect, operational budget she can rewrite over a special law; the RN need only abstain for the budget to pass
political_alpha.poll_runoffs: Le Pen beats Philippe 57-43 and Melenchon 69-31 (Harris Interactive, 28 September 2026)
political_alpha.ratings: Moody's Aa3 negative outlook; Scope downgraded France in the week of 28 September 2026
political_alpha.lagarde_30_sept: debt approaching 120% of GDP with no clear path to control it is a serious problem (La Croix, 30 September 2026)
political_alpha.scenarios: RN stands aside and the budget passes in December (slightly more likely); RN hardens and the government falls; a market crisis removes the room for a deal

scope_downgrade.source: Bloomberg, 18 September 2026 (Political Alpha's note gives only 'Scope Ratings downgraded France last week'); checked 2026-10-07

cour_des_comptes_2025.source: Cour des comptes, report on the financial situation and outlook of the pension system, 20 February 2025 (figures as reported by previssima.fr); added 2026-10-07 for slide 13

wsj_bond_trade_backfired.source: Wall Street Journal, Joe Wallace, 'How the French Bond Trade Backfired on Investors', early October 2026 (the print-to-PDF carries no date; the text describes the selloff of Thursday 1 and Friday 2 October 2026). docs/research/wsj-french-bond-trade-backfired-2026-10.pdf; received from Charlie 2026-10-07
wsj_bond_trade_backfired.attribution: forced selling and the unwind of levered carry trades (SMBC, Pimco, PGIM quoted); 5-year spreads widened more than 10-year, which PGIM's Tipp reads as forced selling rather than a change in creditworthiness
wsj_bond_trade_backfired.swap_spread_trade: buying French and Italian 2- to 5-year bonds against paying on swaps was a popular trade that went the wrong way on Thursday; German bonds outperformed swaps the same day (Morgan Stanley)
wsj_bond_trade_backfired.roll_down_noted: L&G's managers saw the roll-down (a 5-year bond becoming a 4-year bond with a narrower spread) as a source of return but held off because too many investors were still long France

wsj_magic_money_debt_bomb.source: Wall Street Journal, Stacy Meichtry and Chelsey Dulaney, 'France's Appetite for Magic Money Has Turned Into a Debt Bomb', early October 2026 ('last week' = the selloff of 1-2 October). docs/research/wsj-france-magic-money-debt-bomb-2026-10.pdf; received from Charlie 2026-10-07
wsj_magic_money_debt_bomb.debt_service_source: study commissioned by the French finance ministry
wsj_magic_money_debt_bomb.le_pen_retirement_age: as low as 60, costing an extra EUR 9bn a year by her account
wsj_magic_money_debt_bomb.banque_de_france: no longer buying government bonds; portfolio shrinking as bonds mature
wsj_magic_money_debt_bomb.selloff_amplifier: the sudden unwind of risky hedge-fund trades that had grown popular in recent months

ft_global_bond_rout_2026_10_01.source: Financial Times, Herbert, Smith, Sandlund and Lewis, 'Eurozone borrowing costs surge in global bond rout', 1 October 2026. docs/research/eurozone-borrowing-costs-surge-global-bond-rout-2026-10.pdf; received from Charlie 2026-10-07
ft_global_bond_rout_2026_10_01.us_10y_note: highest in almost a quarter of a century; closed 5.24
ft_global_bond_rout_2026_10_01.uk_30y_gilt: above 6% for the first time since 1998
ft_global_bond_rout_2026_10_01.driver: the Iran war's energy shock on public finances; inflation prints above expectations in Germany, France and Italy
ft_global_bond_rout_2026_10_01.unwinds: hedge funds and other big investors forced to ditch long-term debt or unwind lossmaking trades (RBC BlueBay's Bell: 'lots of people are getting stopped out of long positions')
ft_global_bond_rout_2026_10_01.budget: the 2027 budget put forward the same day with EUR 43bn of cuts and tax increases

ft_france_replaces_italy_2026_08_27.source: Financial Times, Herbert, Wright, Hodgson, Kazmin and Jones, 'France replaces Italy as European bond investors' biggest worry', 27 August 2026. docs/research/france-replaces-italy-bond-investors-biggest-worry-2026-10.pdf
ft_france_replaces_italy_2026_08_27.pension_reform: the 2026 budget passed only after Lecornu agreed to suspend the retirement-age reform until after 2027
ft_france_replaces_italy_2026_08_27.japanese_investors: decreasing their allocation to French bonds (Mizuho)
ft_france_replaces_italy_2026_08_27.worst_market_outcome: a Melenchon versus Le Pen run-off (Mizuho's Gomez-Liechti)

ft_editorial_fiscal_reality_2026_10_01.source: Financial Times editorial board, 'France meets fiscal reality with a crunch', 1 October 2026. docs/research/france-meets-fiscal-reality-with-a-crunch-2026-10.pdf
ft_editorial_fiscal_reality_2026_10_01.france_10y_pct: above 4.9, the highest in the eurozone, from 3.6 in early July
ft_editorial_fiscal_reality_2026_10_01.oat_bund_spread_bp: more than 125, the highest since the 2012 peak
ft_editorial_fiscal_reality_2026_10_01.budget: EUR 54bn of savings including EUR 43bn of new measures; deficit from 5.4% to 5%, the target missed for 2026
ft_editorial_fiscal_reality_2026_10_01.commission_2030: deficit 6.8% of GDP by 2030 on current policies; debt service EUR 124bn in 2030, 60% more than defence
ft_editorial_fiscal_reality_2026_10_01.philippe: proposes retirement at 65 and a 45-year contribution period
ft_editorial_fiscal_reality_2026_10_01.le_pen: 3% deficit ceiling by 2032 without a plan for the ~EUR 140bn of annual savings needed
ft_editorial_fiscal_reality_2026_10_01.ecb: investors expect the ECB to intervene in a crisis since France is too big to fail; it has the tools; it would face opposition in other capitals to bailing out a country that has repeatedly failed to get its house in order

ft_moulin_ecb_not_needed_2026_10_07.source: Financial Times, Sarah White, 'French central bank chief says ECB intervention not needed to ease bond rout', 7 October 2026. docs/research/french-central-bank-chief-ecb-intervention-not-needed-2026-10.pdf
ft_moulin_ecb_not_needed_2026_10_07.quote: The conditions are not in place now for an intervention by the ECB ... it is here to fight against inflation
ft_moulin_ecb_not_needed_2026_10_07.warning: France risks being 'strangled by interest rates' (to the FT, 5 October 2026)
ft_moulin_ecb_not_needed_2026_10_07.melenchon: called Moulin's warning an 'act of treason' on X; Moulin: 'I will not be intimidated'
ft_moulin_ecb_not_needed_2026_10_07.le_pen: called on the ECB to intervene once public finances are on the mend; presented the RN's budget plan on 6 October
ft_moulin_ecb_not_needed_2026_10_07.oat_bund_spread_pp: almost 1.4, after briefly above 1.5 the week before

interest_bill_2026_09_11.oat_bund_pp: more than 0.9, widest since 2012, wider than Italy and Greece

unhedged_2026_09_02.note: OMT and TPI never used; France would be an awkward test case

far_left_fire_plan_2026_09_24.oat_bund: above 1 point for the first time since the euro crisis
far_left_fire_plan_2026_09_24.lagarde: legally, technically, financially: really not a good idea
far_left_fire_plan_2026_09_24.lfi_clarification: convert to perpetual zero-coupon bonds, Europe-wide, not unilateral (Coquerel)
far_left_fire_plan_2026_09_24.blanchard: without the ECB's accord, very certainly a euro crisis; cancelling shifts the hole to the Banque de France

vanguard_2026_09_30.france_minus_italy_pp: more than 0.2, a record since the 1990s
vanguard_2026_09_30.koutny: a long-term degrading credit; 1.5 points a strong possibility
vanguard_2026_09_30.royal_london: buying the dip; some price action driven by investors forced to sell at internal risk limits
vanguard_2026_09_30.hsbc_attfield: France's debt the cheapest since at least 2008

le_pen_2026_10_06.golden_rule: debt capped at 60% of GDP, deficit cut 0.5% a year, by referendum
le_pen_2026_10_06.pension_claim_bn: 15 to 20, disputed given retirement at 60 for early starters
le_pen_2026_10_06.ecb: called on the ECB to lighten the interest burden once France takes back control

big_read_2026_10_06.oat_bund_pp: around 1.4, up almost two-thirds in a month
big_read_2026_10_06.corporates_below_sovereign: more than a quarter of IG French companies (Goldman)
big_read_2026_10_06.moscovici: too big to fail, but not too big for the markets to punish
big_read_2026_10_06.tpi: ECB declined to intervene in summer 2022 at an Italian spread of 2.5 points; TPI requires sound and sustainable policies

moulin_2026_10_05.france_10y: close to 5% on Friday 2 October, 4.86% on Monday 5 October
